title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Following preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent reused for both episodes), we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 paired intents and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic validator; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition actually run. All run artifacts and analysis outputs are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent-to-configuration translators for network operations (NetOps). Stochastic generation can introduce operational risk—syntax errors, ordering mistakes, and vendor-specific subtleties—that deterministic checks or human oversight are intended to mitigate. Prior surveys and empirical studies show LLMs can produce draft configurations under controlled conditions but emphasize the need for mechanized verification or human review [1],[2].

A common architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline: produce a candidate, run a deterministic validator, and when failures are detected attempt bounded repairs before acceptance [3],[4]. Although prior work demonstrates that GVR reduces mechanically verifiable error classes, it remains unclear how large the marginal verifier/repair benefit is when modern LLMs already produce largely validator-conforming outputs for constrained tasks. This uncertainty is compounded by evaluation heterogeneity (emulation vs production) and by mixed evidence about LLM-only self-correction [5],[6].

Research question and contributions. We ask: When the same natural-language intent is realized by a single LLM-generated configuration candidate and checked by a deterministic verifier, how large is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction between baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (validator + up-to-one automated repair) episodes? To answer this we executed a preregistered paired experiment (shared_initial_candidate semantics) with N_pairs = 250 intents. Contributions: (1) a sealed preregistered paired measurement isolating the marginal verifier+single-repair effect on identical candidates; (2) complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation for generator/repair stages; (3) quantitative inference (paired difference, exact McNemar p, bootstrap CI) and artifact-grounded discussion of interpretation and limits.
sections.related_work:
LLM-to-configuration work and surveys demonstrate practical interest and mixed empirical outcomes: several studies report that LLMs can create usable draft device configurations in emulation or constrained testbeds, but many note remaining syntax/semantic errors and the need for verification [1],[2],[7]. Deterministic validators and formal tools (e.g., Batfish-like analyses, header-space approaches, model checking) are established methods for mechanized checks of forwarding, reachability, and local-policy properties and are often proposed as validator components in GVR pipelines [3],[8].

Generate–verify and generate–repair architectures are established in code and configuration domains; evaluations show these pipelines reduce mechanically checkable defects but leave deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties unresolved [4],[9]. Work on prompt-injection and retrieval-based attacks highlights security risks for LLM-integrated applications and motivates filtering and validation layers, though adaptive adversary evaluations in NetOps pipelines remain underexplored [10].

This study differs by applying a preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics (identical initial candidate reused across conditions), reporting full deterministic reconciliation of provider-call stages, and archiving validator traces and repair artifacts enabling audit of the numeric outcomes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered (study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1). Confirmatory design: paired binary comparison on N_pairs = 250 intents under shared_initial_candidate semantics and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Analysis plan: exact two-sided McNemar for paired outcomes and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration froze inclusion/exclusion, single-repair policy, and maximum model-call budget.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded an initial_state, expected_final_state, a required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow constraints (examples: make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU change). Tasks were intentionally constrained to reduce ambiguity and exercise workflow-dependent ordering.

Model invocation and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The declared model for initial generation was gpt-5-mini. Per the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, we produced exactly one initial generation per intent and reused that same candidate for both the baseline and guarded episodes; no independent per-condition first-pass generations were produced. The execution accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251, reflecting 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair-stage generation (single repair exercised during the run). This stage mapping isolates the marginal effect of validation and the single permitted repair on identical model outputs.

Guarded pipeline, deterministic validator, and repair policy. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to a deterministic validator implementing full intent-constraint validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering, validating workflow/group constraints, and comparing resulting final_state snapshots to task expectations. If validator.valid == false for a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair limited to syntactic and ordering fixes (e.g., reorder commands to match required_sequence, split multi-command lines). Repaired candidates were re-submitted exactly once; no multi-iteration repairs or human escalation were permitted.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. Exclusions were defined for items that prevented deterministic verification (e.g., vendor-parser failures) or contained credential-like tokens or denylist matches. Contamination detectors would flag embedded instruction-like tokens; flagged items were to be excluded from the primary analysis and addressed in sensitivity analyses. In the executed confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged; complete_pair_count = 250.

Confirmatory analysis executor. The primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary analysis: exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All analysis inputs and outputs were archived.
sections.results:
Execution summary and reconciliation. The run completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250 and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). No episodes were excluded and no contamination flags occurred in the confirmatory partition.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency was n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call: repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference, computed with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729, is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). The point estimate is +0.4 percentage points (0.004).

Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to the task required_command_count and final_state snapshots matching expected_final_state. Hard-difficulty tasks required multi-command sequences and dependency rules; representative validator traces for such tasks show complete parsing and no violation codes in passed episodes. The only repair exercised applied a deterministic ordering/syntactic fix that converted the single failing candidate to a validated pass.

Missingness, exclusions, and repairs. No confirmatory episodes were excluded for parser failure, contamination, or verifier runtime error. Only one automated repair call occurred during the confirmatory run; it resolved the sole baseline failure. Sensitivity analyses treating excluded or missing pairs as failures are moot for the executed partition because no exclusions occurred.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational meaning. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained emulation-style tasks executed, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of adding a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the only failing candidate via the single allowed repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the maximum verifier-detected improvement under these conditions.

Reasons for the small observed gain. Artifact-grounded explanations include: (1) constrained, deterministic task design reduced intent ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model produced highly consistent syntactically valid sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final-state snapshot) but not broader live-protocol or emergent multi-device semantics.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to target a 15 percentage-point detectable effect. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed, which reduces power to detect small absolute improvements; therefore the bootstrap CI bounding the maximum plausible verifier benefit is the most informative result here.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and validator encoding. Construct validity: deterministic validation captures mechanically checkable correctness but not runtime protocol dynamics or vendor-fidelity beyond the validator model. External validity: the executed confirmatory evidence covers the synthetic/emulation partition only; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not evaluated.

Operational implications and caution. These results should not be interpreted to mean validators or repairs are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts. Validator scope, multi-iteration repair, human escalation policies, production heterogeneity, and attacker models can materially change the benefit calculus. The principal, evidence-backed claim here is a bound on the marginal verifier-detected improvement for identical LLM candidates in a constrained emulation partition.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment (shared_initial_candidate semantics) to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. For N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks produced by gpt-5-mini, the initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the permitted single repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; McNemar p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand and inference reported here apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition actually run. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. Execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement for audit and reproducibility.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and execution summary: declared model used for initial generation = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator implementation used for evaluation = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Confirmatory execution completed 500 episodes (250 paired intents) with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generation calls + 1 repair call); stage accounting recorded 250 shared initial-generation events and 1 repair-stage generation.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Executed estimand and deviations: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported in this paper is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). All execution and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript (raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, execution manifest, and analysis outputs) are archived in the study evidence bundle and available for audit per the track's artifact policy.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final-state snapshot) but did not measure runtime protocol-level correctness or emergent multi-device interactions.
Only one declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
